raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`Qwen25Detector` (parsers `qwen`, `qwen25`, and the `trinity` subclass) finds tool calls in `detect_and_parse` with

```python
re.findall(rf"{re.escape(bot)}(.*?){re.escape(eot)}", text, re.DOTALL)
```

When the closing `\n</tool_call>` never arrives, each opening tag rescans to the end of the text, so the cost is quadratic:

| Input (repeated `<tool_call>\n `) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 25 KB | 0.80 s | < 0.1 ms |
| 50 KB | 3.6 s | 0.1 ms |
| 101 KB | 12.6 s | 0.2 ms |

Tool-call parsing runs synchronously on the tokenizer manager's event loop, so one such response stalls every in-flight request. Found with an Atheris fuzzing harness that records per-input parse time.

## Modifications

- `_iter_tool_call_bodies`: a linear `str.find` scan yielding exactly the bodies `findall` returned (the closer is searched for from the end of the opener, so the shared `\n` behaves as in the regex). The now-unused `import re` is removed.
- Regression test `TestQwen25Detector::test_detect_and_parse_unclosed_tags_in_linear_time`: 74.2 s on `main`, fast here.

## Accuracy Tests

- Differential test of `main` vs patched `qwen25` and `trinity` (old `trinity` loaded against the old base), comparing `detect_and_parse` and every streaming result under random re-chunking: **0 mismatches** over 40k random plus 40k mutated well-formed inputs (about 25k produced parsed calls).
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/`: 630 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See the table above.

Note: streaming for this detector goes through `BaseFormatDetector.parse_streaming_increment`, which re-parses the whole buffer with `partial_json_parser` on every chunk while a JSON body is unclosed. That is O(n) per chunk (about 259 ms per chunk at 89 KB) and affects every detector built on the base class. Fixing it needs incremental JSON parsing, so it is left for a separate change.

Related: #42573, #42574, #42575, #42576, #42577 (same issue class in other tool-call parsers).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -1,6 +1,5 @@
 import json
 import logging
-import re
 from typing import List
 
 from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Tool
@@ -40,6 +39,18 @@ def __init__(self):
         self.tool_call_separator = "\n"
         self._normal_text_buffer = ""  # Buffer for handling partial end tokens
 
+    def _iter_tool_call_bodies(self, text: str):
+        # Linear scan on purpose: a `<tool_call>\n(.*?)\n</tool_call>` findall
+        # rescans to the end from every opening tag when the end tag never arrives.
+        start = text.find(self.bot_token)
+        while start != -1:
+            body_start = start + len(self.bot_token)
+            end = text.find(self.eot_token, body_start)
+            if end == -1:
+                return
+            yield text[body_start:end]
+            start = text.find(self.bot_token, end + len(self.eot_token))
+
     def has_tool_call(self, text: str) -> bool:
         """Check if the text contains a Qwen 2.5 format tool call."""
         return self.bot_token in text
@@ -57,9 +68,7 @@ def detect_and_parse(self, text: str, tools: List[Tool]) -> StreamingParseResult
         if self.bot_token not in text:
             return StreamingParseResult(normal_text=normal_text, calls=[])
 
-        # Find all <tool_call>\n...\n</tool_call> blocks
-        pattern = rf"{re.escape(self.bot_token)}(.*?){re.escape(self.eot_token)}"
-        match_result_list = re.findall(pattern, text, re.DOTALL)
+        match_result_list = list(self._iter_tool_call_bodies(text))
         calls = []
         for match_result in match_result_list:
             try:

@@ -1,5 +1,6 @@
 import functools
 import json
+import time
 import unittest
 import warnings
 
@@ -5288,6 +5289,22 @@ def test_detect_and_parse_with_normal_text_prefix(self):
         self.assertEqual(len(result.calls), 1)
         self.assertIn("let me check", result.normal_text)
 
+    def test_detect_and_parse_unclosed_tags_in_linear_time(self):
+        """Many opening tags without a closing tag must not stall the parser
+        (it runs on the event loop); earlier complete calls still parse."""
+        text = (
+            '<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_current_weather", "arguments": {"city": "NYC", "state": "NY", "unit": "celsius"}}\n</tool_call>'
+            + "<tool_call>\n " * 20000
+        )
+
+        start = time.perf_counter()
+        result = self.detector.detect_and_parse(text, self.tools)
+        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
+
+        self.assertLess(elapsed, 1.0)
+        self.assertEqual(len(result.calls), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result.calls[0].parameters)["city"], "NYC")
+
     # -- Streaming tests --
